key_insight: Frozen medical LLM embeddings can act as a shared space that combines structured EHR variables and discharge notes to predict primary ICD category more accurately than single-modality or baseline models.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a lightweight way to reuse existing clinical representations for diagnosis coding, multimodal EHR analysis, and cross-dataset adaptation with limited new labels.
method: Built a MIMIC-IV cohort of 13,645 admissions from the 10 most frequent primary ICD-10 codes, merged into seven categories.
Serialized structured variables into text and combined them with leakage-pruned discharge notes.
Extracted hidden states from five layers of a frozen MedFound-Llama3-8B-finetuned model and trained linear probes, plus a compact adapter for MIMIC-III transfer.
evidence_signal: On MIMIC-IV, the combined probe achieved 87.69% strict accuracy and 91.45% medical accuracy, outperforming single-modality probes and baseline methods.
watch_item: Results depend on careful leakage pruning and dataset-specific label structure, so performance may not transfer directly to other hospitals or coding setups.
paper_title: Primary ICD Category Prediction using LLM-based Probing
